payload.rationale: Observed: as of 18 Sep 2026 (21 UTC) the NHC summary lists five named storms, zero hurricanes, zero major hurricanes and ACE of only 4.4 — an extraordinarily quiet season through the climatological peak (Sept 10). Resolution requires at least four Category 3+ hurricanes before Dec 1, so all four must form in roughly the final ten weeks. Climatologically (1991–2020 mean of three majors per full season), only about one to 1.5 majors on average form after mid-September; seasons producing four or more majors after Sept 18 are rare (my recollection: roughly 2020 and 2024 in the last ~25 years, i.e., on the order of 10% unconditionally). Conditioning on a season with no hurricane at all by Sept 18 — which is nearly unprecedented in the satellite era and implies persistent suppressive conditions (likely El Niño-type shear, stable/dry air, or unfavorable SST patterns) — lowers this further, though late-season Caribbean/Gulf outbursts (e.g., 2020's Delta/Eta/Iota, 2024's Milton/Rafael) show back-loaded bursts are possible. I estimate roughly 4%. Too low if: the quiet start reflects transient factors (e.g., unfavorable MJO phase, Saharan dust) rather than a seasonal regime, and very warm Caribbean/Gulf waters support a 2020/2024-style late burst; also retrospective upgrades in post-season reports could add majors. Too high if: the underlying suppression (e.g., a developing El Niño) persists through October–November, making even one major hurricane unlikely, as in seasons like 2013 or 2006 that ended with few or no late majors.
limitations: No current basin forecast, ENSO state, SST anomalies, or CSU/NOAA updated outlooks were supplied; the conditioning on 'quiet start' relies on general background recall of past seasons, which may be imperfect.
Historical analog counts for post-Sept-18 major hurricanes are from memory and approximate, not a fitted model.
Source excerpts were search-index snapshots (direct NHC pages returned 403), and post-season reanalysis could revise storm intensities before settlement.
Whether operational or post-season best-track classification governs resolution is not fully specified.
